title: Research Literacy, Treatment Limits and Evidence-Based Cultivation
summary: Evidence-based cultivation depends on understanding what a study actually tested, how strongly its design supports a conclusion and whether the population, treatment and environment match the decision being made.

sections.title: A treatment result is not a universal target
sections.body: Cannabis studies often evaluate particular cultivars, substrates, nutrient concentrations, lighting systems or environments. A statistically significant difference within that experiment supports a conclusion about those conditions, not automatic transfer of the exact treatment value to every production system.

sections.title: Replication separates patterns from anecdotes
sections.body: Repeated biological units and independent trials help estimate variability and distinguish consistent response from one plant or one room event. Breeding, nutrition and environmental decisions become more defensible when measurements are standardized and repeated.

sections.title: Source type affects what a claim can support
sections.body: Peer-reviewed experiments, reviews, government standards, university extension and industry technical documents can each contribute useful information, but they answer different questions. Strong educational content identifies the source and preserves uncertainty instead of flattening all evidence into equal authority.
